ety.text: From анти- (anti-) + обще́ственный (obščéstvennyj), a calque of French antisocial. First attested in the 1900s.
From бес- (bes-) + па́ртия (pártija) + -ный (-nyj), a calque of German parteilos. First attested in 1901.

ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dьrgati (“to pull, to comb (flax)?”).
Borrowed from Arabic قَلَم (qalam), derived from Ancient Greek κάλαμος (kálamos, “reed”).

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic муринъ (murinŭ), ultimately from Latin Maurus. Cognates include Polish Murzyn, Ukrainian му́рин (múryn), Belarusian му́рын (múryn). Doublet of мавр (mavr).

s.g: monsoon (any of a number of winds associated with regions where most rain falls during a particular season)

ety.text: Borrowed from French mousson, from Portuguese monção, from Arabic مَوْسِم (mawsim, “season”), from وَسَمَ (wasama, “to mark, to brand”).

s.g: to pump, to pressurize, to inflate

ety.text: From нагнет- (nagnet-) + -а́ть (-átʹ). Compare Kashubian nagniatac, Polish nagniatać, and Silesian nagniŏtać.

s.g: to hint (at), to allude, to imply (refer to something indirectly or by suggestion)
to wind around, to wrap around

ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ploskъ. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“thin, flat”).
Nominalisation of подлежа́щий (podležáščij), present participle of подлежа́ть (podležátʹ). Calque of Latin subiectum.
Derived from Late Latin potentiālis, likely through German Potenzial.

s.g: carriageway (part of a road that carries traffic)

himself/herself/themselves, in the flesh, in person (used to emphasise that someone encountered is a given person)

ety.text: Acronym of тороида́льная ка́мера с магни́тными кату́шками (toroidálʹnaja kámera s magnítnymi katúškami, “toroidal chamber with magnetic coils”).

x: Приложе́ние и́ли неприложе́ние христиа́нского пра́вила к своему́ слу́чаю был вопро́с сли́шком тру́дный, о кото́ром нельзя́ бы́ло говори́ть слегка́, и вопро́с э́тот был уже́ давно́ решён Алексе́ем Алекса́ндровичем отрица́тельно.
